claims.text: Adding a small amount of tungsten to a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy will promote tungsten-rich nanoprecipitate formation.
The tungsten-rich nanoprecipitates will be coherent with the alloy matrix.
Coherent tungsten-rich nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Coherent tungsten-rich nanoprecipitates will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will reduce elevated-temperature creep rates.
The tungsten-containing alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than an otherwise identical tungsten-free alloy.
The tungsten-containing alloy will have greater creep resistance than an otherwise identical tungsten-free alloy.
The proposed base material contains titanium and nickel as primary constituents plus at least three additional elements, each at 5–35 at%.
The starting alloy is intended to have a largely homogeneous as-cast or solution-treated microstructure.
The proposed operating temperature range is approximately 600–1000°C.
The intervention is limited to conditions under which the relevant elevated-temperature phases remain stable.
Processing conditions that cause unwanted phase separation should be avoided.
